scope: Targeted primary-source contribution review within Franka/pinned-FORGE peg-then-gear recovery. Not an exhaustive systematic review or a claim that the remaining question is absent from all literature.

supersedes_scope.clarification: Earlier bounded assessment omitted close assembly-curriculum predecessors. Its record and hashes remain unchanged; this review controls prospective contribution and campaign decisions.

sources.title: Recovery-Focused Dynamic Curriculum TD3 for Robotic Peg-in-Hole Insertion Skill
sources.access: Institutional metadata and abstract read; publisher/full text unavailable in this check.
sources.locator: Abstract, especially difficulty regimes and scheduler paragraphs
sources.established_overlap: Simulated recovery-oriented peg insertion; success-dependent redistribution across three difficulty classes, easier-case retention, and comparisons against non-curricular and static training.
sources.consequence: Closest direct overlap. The broad recovery-plus-adaptive-selection proposal is already represented in prior work.
sources.unresolved_details: Exact scheduler, contact witness, dwell, force abort timing, grasp constraints, budgets and independent seed treatment cannot be determined from this abstract. Do not assert those features are absent.

sources.title: Accelerating Robot Learning of Contact-Rich Manipulations: A Curriculum Learning Study
sources.access: Primary full text, sections III-E/F and IV-A/E inspected.
sources.established_overlap: Industrial insertion with curriculum-controlled randomization; fixed and performance-adaptive schedules, uniform/Gaussian sampling, three training repeats, unseen conditions and real-robot evaluation.
sources.important_credit: Already includes force-triggered termination, success and time comparisons. Its reported mean completion times omit failures; dynamic reward is studied separately.
sources.difference_to_test: Keep our reward, geometry and force/dwell criteria fixed while changing sampling, report time per request including failures, and evaluate completion after a common witnessed stall. These are benchmark choices, not proof of field-wide novelty.

sources.title: IndustReal: Transferring Contact-Rich Assembly Tasks from Simulation to Reality
sources.established_overlap: Success-dependent sampling of assembly start heights, with stage advances/reversions and comparison to standard/no curriculum on peg and gear assembly.
sources.difference_to_test: Its studied curriculum includes partial engagement at initialization. Our primary jobs start from a valid retained grasp above the fixture and select fixed fault bins. This operating constraint does not make adaptive sampling new.

sources.title: AutoMate: Specialist and Generalist Assembly Policies over Diverse Geometries
sources.established_overlap: Uses IndustReal sampling curricula during assembly fine-tuning, alongside demonstrations, imitation and diverse geometries.
sources.consequence: Neither applying a curriculum to assembly nor scaling beyond one geometry is new.

sources.title: FORGE: Force-Guided Exploration for Robust Contact-Rich Manipulation under Uncertainty
sources.access: Primary full text inspected; installed task remains pinned.
sources.established_overlap: Force-aware learned search/assembly, dynamics randomization, success prediction and real-robot peg/gear/nut tasks.
sources.consequence: Credit the base manipulation method. Our finite-job adapter is enabling engineering; a scripted retry is not a substitute for a competent upstream learned reference in the full study.

sources.title: Reverse Curriculum Generation for Reinforcement Learning
sources.access: Primary proceedings and full-text sections 4/5 inspected.
sources.established_overlap: Selects intermediate-success starting states, retains old starts and expands feasible starts with action-space exploration; evaluates manipulation.
sources.consequence: The idea behind p*(1-p) is established. Our between-job parameter selection avoids copying contact states but is not a novel principle.

sources.title: Teacher algorithms for curriculum learning of Deep RL in continuously parameterized environments
sources.access: Primary proceedings abstract and paper summary inspected.
sources.established_overlap: Samples environment parameters using absolute learning progress and addresses differing learnability.
sources.consequence: Adding a learning-progress term would also require attribution and controlled comparison, not a novelty claim by renaming it.

sources.title: Prioritized Level Replay
sources.access: Primary proceedings abstract and paper introduction inspected.
sources.established_overlap: Reweights environment instances by estimated learning potential to improve sample efficiency/generalization.
sources.consequence: Selecting useful training situations is an established problem. A new-algorithm claim would need a strong adaptive reference, not only uniform and fixed curricula.

novelty_decision.claim_route: Replication and controlled engineering extension; any useful empirical contribution must still be earned.
not_evidence_of_novelty: Different robot, simulator, PPO instead of TD3, or different thresholds
A p*(1-p) priority or a learning-progress term
A new website, force penalty, extra training, or the existence of learned post-stall completion
novelty_decision.full_text_limit: The 2026 institutional abstract is sufficient to reject a broad first-method claim. It is insufficient to establish exact equivalence or to claim that our accounting requirements are missing from that paper.

precise_unanswered_question: In the pinned Franka assembly benchmark, at the same total charged simulator cost and fixed nominal share, does reallocating the existing fault-bin practice from uniform or a calibrated fixed schedule to recent-outcome-based selection reduce unfinished whole jobs? If so, does it improve prevention, completion after a common witnessed contact stall, or both, and does it offer a practical reliability/time advantage over unchanged scripted retry?
question_scope: Unanswered for this controlled setup. It is not presented as the first investigation of assembly curricula or recovery efficiency.
practical_benefit_to_establish: A measured choice of the simplest controller/training schedule that meets a declared reliability target for the least training cost, with failed jobs and retries included in elapsed time.

An executable, versioned benchmark that exposes false recovery attribution, missing cost, and sensitivity to physics timestep; source, manifests, per-job records and publishable artifacts must support the result.
A documented boundary where adaptive training is unnecessary or fails to improve on uniform/fixed training or retry; no general claim beyond the evaluated tasks and fault support.

existing_evidence.interpretation: A competent insertion policy and post-stall behavior are measured. There is no learned reliability advantage over retry in the confirmation, no curriculum comparison, and no evidence of learned-policy physics robustness.

interpretation: At cohorts 5-6, illustrative p*(1-p) shares span only 16.35-16.82 percent across fault bins, near uniform 16.67 percent. This is weak discrimination at the proposed short-screen budget.
In the last two cohorts, 379 of 384 failures are force aborts and only one contact stall is logged among 2048 jobs. The score cannot be described as identifying recoverable stalls.
These are stochastic changing-policy training logs. Differences from frozen mean evaluation do not establish that exploration noise causes the failures; conditions differ.
A replayed score is not an estimate of how an adaptively trained policy would perform. No sampler advantage or new rollout is inferred.

decision.next: Finish the frozen learned/retry physics validation, then verify and register the bounded peg comparison. Use the small screen to decide whether a larger comparative study is justified; do not buy novelty with more training.

contribution_acceptance: A claimed benefit must survive all-request accounting, matched costs, a competent fixed curriculum and retry, multiple training seeds, and physics checks. A changed reward/geometry invalidates both affected arms.
The existing final target remains halving unfinished jobs versus uniform with no more than two percentage points nominal loss. Report uncertainty; a small development screen cannot establish it.

A two-task result and a mechanism ablation are required for the planned broader claim. Without a useful effect or a well-supported actionable negative boundary, deliver a reproducible technical report and do not assert a novel research contribution.
scope_and_limitations: Prior work already studies sample efficiency, force handling and recovery curricula; the chosen collection of controls is not itself a proven novelty claim.
No final-test seed or reserved combination was sampled, and no training or simulator job ran in this review.
The current frozen withdrawal metric and failed competence gate remain unchanged; the separate post-stall endpoint is retained.

Full text and exact details of the 2026 direct predecessor remain unavailable. Before an exact reproduction or method-superiority claim, obtain primary implementation details; do not infer them from the abstract.
All old results and registrations are retained. The new design is not a launchable protocol and does not unfreeze study.json or upstream source.
